**Tiziano Vecellio** (Italian:[[titˈtsjaːno veˈtʃɛlljo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); c.1488/1490[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-1)–27 August 1576),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-2) Latinized as **Titianus**, hence known in English as **Titian** ( _TISH-ən_), was an Italian Renaissance painter.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-4) The most important artist of Renaissance Venetian painting, he was born in Pieve di Cadore, near Belluno.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Wolf-5)
Titian was one of the most versatile of Italian painters, equally adept with portraits, landscape backgrounds, and mythological and religious subjects. His painting methods, particularly in the application and use of colour, exerted a profound influence not only on painters of the late Italian Renaissance, but on future generations of Western artists.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-6)

His career was successful from the start, and he became sought after by patrons, initially from Venice and its possessions, then joined by the north Italian princes, and finally the Habsburgs and the papacy. Along with Giorgione, he is considered a founder of the Venetian school of Italian Renaissance painting. In 1590, the painter and art theorist Giovanni Paolo Lomazzo described Titian as "the sun amidst small stars not only among the Italians but all the painters of the world".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Wethey1969-7)
During his long life, Titian's artistic manner changed drastically,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-8) but he retained a lifelong interest in colour. Although his mature works may not contain the vivid, luminous tints of his early pieces, they are remarkable and original in their loose brushwork and subtlety of tone.
_A Man with a Quilted Sleeve_, c. 1509, National Gallery, London
The exact date of Titian's birth is uncertain. When he was an old man he claimed in a letter to Philip II of Spain to have been born in 1474, but this seems most unlikely.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-NGC1975-9) Other writers contemporary to his old age give figures that would equate to birth dates between 1473 and after 1482. Although his age at death being 99 was still accepted into the 20th century,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Sohm2007-10) most modern scholars believe a birth date between 1488 and 1490 is likeliest.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018_62-11)

He was the son of Gregorio Vecellio and his wife Lucia, of whom little is known. The Vecellio family was well established in the area, which was ruled by Venice. Titian's grandfather Conte Vecellio was a prominent notary who held a number of offices in the local administration. Three of Conte's sons were notaries, not including Gregorio,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Hope2008-12) who was active as a soldier and closely associated with the Venetian Arsenal,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Joannides2001_7-13) but worked mainly as a timber merchant and also managed mines in the mountainous Cadore region for their owners.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Nichols2013-14) The Vecellio family of Cadore are descended from the LombardDa Camino family through their common ancestor Vecile da Camino.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Crowe2011-15) The Da Camino most likely descend from the Collalto family.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-16)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-18)
Ludovico Dolce, who knew Titian, says that Titian had four masters, the first being Sebastiano Zuccato, the second Gentile Bellini, then his brother Giovanni Bellini, and last, Giorgione. No documentation for these relationships has been found. The Zucatti family of artists are best known as mosaicists, but there is no evidence that the painter Sebastiano Zuccato himself was active as a mosaicist, although Joannides says he probably was.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Joannides2001_10-19)

According to Giorgio Vasari, who also knew Titian and included a not always accurate biography of the artist in his _Lives_, Titian first studied under Giovanni Bellini. Dolce writes that the boy was sent to Venice at age nine, along with his brother Francesco, to live with an uncle and apprentice to Sebastiano Zuccato. Leaving Zuccato, Titian briefly transferred to the studio of Gentile Bellini, one of the largest and most productive workshops in Venice. Following Gentile's death in 1507 he entered into an apprenticeship with Gentile's younger brother Giovanni, acknowledged by contemporaries as the preeminent Venetian painter of the day. As there is no documentation of Titian's work before 1510, there is no way to know which version, Dolce's or Vasari's, is closer to the truth.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018-20) Living in the city, Titian found a group of young men about his own age, among them Giovanni Palma da Serinalta, Lorenzo Lotto, Sebastiano Luciani, and Giorgio da Castelfranco, nicknamed Giorgione.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Gillet1912-21)Francesco Vecellio, Titian's brother, while more workmanlike in his approach to painting and lacking Titian's talent, was able to achieve some notice in his home town of Cadore and the Bellunese area around it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Freedberg1993-22)

His final painting, the _\_Pietà\__, is an image of tragic pathos that evokes feelings of pity and sorrow in the presence of death. It is a highly personalized composition, wherein Titian, portrayed as Saint Jerome, prostrates himself before the Virgin and reaches out to the lifeless body of Christ.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018_210-114) Statues of Moses with the Ten Commandments and the Hellespontine Sibyl, who prophesied Christ's death and resurrection, flank the stone piers of a niche with a semi-dome apse and a mosaic ceiling that depicts a pelican piercing its breast to feed its young[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Nichols2013_7-115) (a symbol of the resurrection), the whole surmounted by a pediment topped with burning lamps.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018_210-114) Mary Magdalene turns away in horror from the scene, unable to bear the sight.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Nichols2013_7-115) The votive tablet in the lower right depicts Titian and his son Orazio praying before a heavenly vision of the Pietà. Behind the tablet is Titian's coat-of-arms with the double-headed Habsburg eagle.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Save_Venice_Piet%C3%A0_2025-116) The canvas, composed of seven pieces of canvas stitched together and measuring 378 centimetres (12.40 ft) x 348 centimetres (11.42 ft), is one of the largest ever painted by Titian. Because the Pietà was to decorate the artist's own tomb, it is often interpreted as an invocation or "painted prayer" for protection from the plague that eventually killed him.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Nygren2015-117)

Titian's estate was in disarray soon after his death. Orazio died only weeks afterwards, leading to a five-year dispute between Titian's other son Pomponio and his son-in-law Cornelio Sarcinelli over the estate, including the contents of the workshop and paintings in the house.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Nygren2015-117) Around 1581, when a settlement was reached between Pomponio and Sarcinelli, Palma il Giovane acquired the painting and held it until his death in 1628. In about 1631 it was installed in the church of Sant’Angelo in Venice, where it remained until 1814, when it became part of the collection of the [Gallerie dell'Accademia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallerie_dell'Accademia "Gallerie dell'Accademia"). According to Robertson, it was not well known until it entered the critical literature in 1909 when Frimmel deemed it a work by the master's hand. Robertson describes its subject as "superficially, at least, repellent", and refers to the "brutality" of its treatment. It has been widely accepted as one of Titian's important later works since the 1930s.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Robertson1983-119) Another violent masterpiece is _Tarquin and Lucretia_.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-120)

Tomb of Titian in Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, Venice
While the plague raged in Venice, Titian died on 27 August 1576.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Kennedy2006-121) Given the modern scholarly consensus that he was born between 1488 and 1490, he would have been at least eighty-six years old, and no more than ninety.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018_62-11) Although in 1575 he had installed his last painting, the _Pietà_, which he designed specifically for his own burial site in the Frari, it was soon removed, and he was buried beneath the Frari's Altar of the Crucifix (Altare del Crocifisso) without the painting in place.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-De_La_Rosa2011-122) According to Nichols, the Franciscan friars of the Frari felt that the painting did not respect the 'ancient devotions' to the medieval crucifix in the Chapel of Christ, and had returned it to him. Very shortly after Titian's death, his son, assistant and sole heir Orazio, also died of the plague, greatly complicating the settlement of his estate, as he had made no will.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-123) The painting apparently remained in his studio and eventually the painter Jacopo Palma il Giovane, who claimed to have been a pupil in his workshop, came into its possession and added a few small touches. After Palma's death in 1628, the church of Sant'Angelo acquired the canvas in 1631, where it remained until the church was destroyed in the early 18th century. The Pietà became part of the collection of the Accademia Galleries in 1814.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Save_Venice_Piet%C3%A0_2025-116)

A large monument to honor Titian at his original burial site was commissioned by the Emperor Ferdinand I of Austria in 1843. Its completion was carried on after his abdication in 1848 by his successor Franz Joseph through 1852.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Catra2017-124) Luigi Zandomeneghi, a student of Antonio Canova, and director of the Accademia when the commission was made, was selected to create the monument. It was built of the finest Carrara marble across the nave from Titian's own [Ca' Pesaro Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_di_Ca'_Pesaro "Madonna di Ca' Pesaro"). Zandomeneghi's sons, Pietro and Andrea, completed the project after he died.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-De_La_Rosa2011-122)

## TITIAN | TIZIAN - Life, Works & Painting Style | Great Artists simply Explained in 3 minutes!
Titian, or actually Tiziano Vecellio, is considered the leading representative of 16th century Venetian painting and one of the main masters of the Italian High Renaissance. Titian was born around 1488 to 1490 in Pieve di Cadore, a small town in the Republic of Venice. He received training from the Bellini brothers as a child, founded his own workshop at the age of around 25 and became a celebrated artist. Emperor Charles V elevated him to the nobility and appointed him court painter. He also traveled to Rome and Augsburg. Titian had two sons with his first wife Cecilia. After her death, he married again and had another daughter, who can also be found in his paintings. It is possible that he had another illegitimate daughter. Titian died of the plague in Venice in 1576 at the advanced age of around 86. Titian's painting style was characterized by a masterful technique and a remarkable sense of color and light. Towards the end of his long life, his work became darker and more impressionistic, probably also influenced by various strokes of fate. He painted portraits as well as landscapes, mythological and religious subjects. His motifs reflected a wide range of human emotions. His three most famous works include: The sensual painting "Venus of Urbino", which became an iconic work in art history due to its elegance and sophistication. In the mythological painting "Bacchus and Ariadne", Titian captures the moment when the god Bacchus falls in love with the beautiful Ariadne with a dynamic composition and vivid colors. And in his haunting self-portrait, painted around fifteen hundred and sixty-two, he shows his artistic maturity. The expression in his eyes and the subtle use of light and shadow testify to his deep understanding of the human psyche. Titian's life's work spans more than seven decades and over 600 works. In 1590, the painter and art theorist Giovanni Paolo Lomazzo described Titian as "the sun amidst small stars not only among the Italians but all the painters of the world".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Wethey1969-7)
During his long life, Titian's artistic manner changed drastically,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-8) but he retained a lifelong interest in colour. Although his mature works may not contain the vivid, luminous tints of his early pieces, they are remarkable and original in their loose brushwork and subtlety of tone.

While the plague raged in Venice, Titian died on 27 August 1576.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Kennedy2006-121) Given the modern scholarly consensus that he was born between 1488 and 1490, he would have been at least eighty-six years old, and no more than ninety.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Cole2018_62-11) Although in 1575 he had installed his last painting, the _Pietà_, which he designed specifically for his own burial site in the Frari, it was soon removed, and he was buried beneath the Frari's Altar of the Crucifix (Altare del Crocifisso) without the painting in place.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-De_La_Rosa2011-122) According to Nichols, the Franciscan friars of the Frari felt that the painting did not respect the 'ancient devotions' to the medieval crucifix in the Chapel of Christ, and had returned it to him. Very shortly after Titian's death, his son, assistant and sole heir Orazio, also died of the plague, greatly complicating the settlement of his estate, as he had made no will.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-123) The painting apparently remained in his studio and eventually the painter Jacopo Palma il Giovane, who claimed to have been a pupil in his workshop, came into its possession and added a few small touches. After Palma's death in 1628, the church of Sant'Angelo acquired the canvas in 1631, where it remained until the church was destroyed in the early 18th century. The Pietà became part of the collection of the Accademia Galleries in 1814.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Save_Venice_Piet%C3%A0_2025-116)
texts.36: A large monument to honor Titian at his original burial site was commissioned by the Emperor Ferdinand I of Austria in 1843. Its completion was carried on after his abdication in 1848 by his successor Franz Joseph through 1852.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-Catra2017-124) Luigi Zandomeneghi, a student of Antonio Canova, and director of the Accademia when the commission was made, was selected to create the monument. It was built of the finest Carrara marble across the nave from Titian's own [Ca' Pesaro Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_di_Ca'_Pesaro "Madonna di Ca' Pesaro"). Zandomeneghi's sons, Pietro and Andrea, completed the project after he died.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titian#cite_note-De_La_Rosa2011-122)

## TITIAN | TIZIAN - Life, Works & Painting Style | Great Artists simply Explained in 3 minutes!
Titian, or actually Tiziano Vecellio, is considered the leading representative of 16th century Venetian painting and one of the main masters of the Italian High Renaissance. Titian was born around 1488 to 1490 in Pieve di Cadore, a small town in the Republic of Venice. He received training from the Bellini brothers as a child, founded his own workshop at the age of around 25 and became a celebrated artist. Emperor Charles V elevated him to the nobility and appointed him court painter. He also traveled to Rome and Augsburg. Titian had two sons with his first wife Cecilia. After her death, he married again and had another daughter, who can also be found in his paintings. It is possible that he had another illegitimate daughter. Titian died of the plague in Venice in 1576 at the advanced age of around 86. Titian's painting style was characterized by a masterful technique and a remarkable sense of color and light. Towards the end of his long life, his work became darker and more impressionistic, probably also influenced by various strokes of fate. He painted portraits as well as landscapes, mythological and religious subjects. His motifs reflected a wide range of human emotions. His three most famous works include: The sensual painting "Venus of Urbino", which became an iconic work in art history due to its elegance and sophistication. In the mythological painting "Bacchus and Ariadne", Titian captures the moment when the god Bacchus falls in love with the beautiful Ariadne with a dynamic composition and vivid colors. And in his haunting self-portrait, painted around fifteen hundred and sixty-two, he shows his artistic maturity. The expression in his eyes and the subtle use of light and shadow testify to his deep understanding of the human psyche. Titian's life's work spans more than seven decades and over 600 works. He was one of the most prolific Italian painters of his time. His works influenced not only artists of his time, but also subsequent generations, including Rubens, Watteau and Delacroix.…...more
